evidence:
STATIC DESIGN REVIEW: no ranking inversion found. (1) tests/scoring.toml and tests/tools/score.py are byte-identical to the frozen template (diff empty): '[gates] render = 0.0 / constraints = 0.0', '[weights] functional = 0.6 / polish = 0.2 / visual = 0.2', '[floors] functional = 0.05'. Function (0.6) outweighs craft (0.4). (2) All per-criterion weights are positive: functional 42 criteria, weights in {1.0,1.5,2.0}, total 58.5; polish 6 x 1.0; visual 3 likert x 1.0; gates 1 + 2 binary all_pass. No criterion rewards the absence of a feature without a control, so an app that passes a strict subset of another app's criteria cannot outscore it. (3) The render gate was reduced to load-and-type (gates/render/judge.toml:23 'This checks only that the app is running and its editor accepts typing ... Do not press Run'), and Run moved to scored cw_basic_run_output; this removes the inversion seen on the earlier candidate, where an app with a broken Run was zeroed at the gate. The three in-dimension gates restate the same load-and-type test (scored/*/prompt.md line 5), so they cannot zero an app the real gate passed. (4) app_context.md:107 'Run may be broken in a submitted app. Criteria that do not depend on Run are still scored on their own steps' keeps editor credit independent of Run. (5) Absence-tolerant wording was checked for inversion: polish cw_controls_keyboard_and_focus says 'A control the app does not have at all is scored elsewhere, not here'; removing Find/Replace to dodge one polish miss (0.2/6 = 0.0333) costs four functional criteria of weight 5.0 (0.6*5/58.5 = 0.0513), and removing Format costs 4.5 weight (0.0462) plus two more polish criteria, so the feature-complete app still ranks higher (thin margin 0.018 for Find/Replace). cw_undo_redo_availability fails 'if the app has no visible Undo and Redo controls'. (6) Floor: reward is 0 unless functional > 0.05, i.e. more than 2.925 of 58.5 weight, so typing-only shells cannot farm polish/visual. (7) Likert normalisation observed on the earlier hosted run is (raw-1)/4 (raw 5 -> 1.0, raw 4 -> 0.75), monotone; the 0 anchor follows the template.

BOUNDED OBSERVATIONS (not defects of this row, recorded for the owner): (a) Per-criterion mass: one polish binary is worth 0.0333 reward and one visual likert step 0.0167, while a functional criterion is worth 0.0103 (w1.0), 0.0154 (w1.5) or 0.0205 (w2.0). So an app with all 42 functional passing, polish 2/6 and visual 3,3,3 scores 0.7667, while an app failing 13 runtime-safety and concurrency criteria (21.5 weight; functional 0.632) with polish 6/6 and visual 5,5,5 scores 0.779. This follows from the template-fixed 0.6/0.2/0.2 shares with 42 vs 6 vs 3 criteria and is not a strict-dominance inversion; it belongs to row 44. (b) gates/constraints cw_shared_saved_record says 'see that the app reports the Save as successful' while its Fails list names only missing/differing/disappearing records; with the gate prompt's 'if a step could not be performed ... fail that criterion', a judge could zero an otherwise complete app whose Save succeeds silently (a miss otherwise worth one polish criterion). Low likelihood because the library entry appearing is itself a report. (c) cw_history_restore_retry lets the judge 'leave this one step out without failing' when the restore is not a replayable request, so a non-idempotent app using a non-recordable transport passes where an equally non-idempotent fetch-based app fails; equal-quality apps, not better-versus-worse.

MEASUREMENT: every artifact hash in raw-evidence-index.json was recomputed and matches (22/22). The scripted golden results on these bytes show all 3 gate, 42 functional and 6 polish checks true, which is one point, not an ordering. The only judge-measured ordering (Oracle 0.9833 > nop 0 = model 0) is on an EARLIER candidate (QC input 4f93c627) whose render gate differed, and its model score was a gate zero, so no scored ordering between two non-trivial apps has ever been measured. qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md requires a hash-bound runtime record for reward ordering before local clearance ('Evidence from mutated weak apps helps with discrimination and ranking'); none exists for input 3f132f27. Functional judge completion within the 9000 s timeout for a feature-rich app (which needs more judge work than a fail-fast broken app) is likewise unmeasured on these bytes; the earlier Oracle trial took about 42 minutes in total. The skill forbids upgrading an unmeasured claim to Pass, hence Not exercised with risk=true.
suggested_fix: No task edit is required for this row from static review. To clear it: record a configured-judge run on these exact bytes for the golden plus at least two mutated weaker apps (for example golden with Run disabled, and golden with Save conflict handling removed) and confirm golden > weaker > gate-failing. Optional tightening: in cw_shared_saved_record state that any visible sign of the Save (such as the entry appearing in the library) counts as the report.
